title: Two copper parts, one sealed enclosure
bullets: Existing RevB copper body and coolant cover
Cover moves away to expose the mating face
speech: These are our existing copper cooling body and coolant cover, shown using their actual CAD geometry. Instead of sealing this interface with eight O rings, we can redesign it as a permanently brazed joint.

title: The outside bond contains the water
speech: With the cover hidden, the blue area shows the water pocket. The gold ring marks the proposed outer bond region. A continuous braze here closes the outside edge, but it is only part of the seal.

title: Each magnet well needs its own bond
bullets: Six outer wells plus one center well
Water surrounds these dry copper islands
An outside seam alone is insufficient
speech: Water also surrounds the seven dry magnet wells. Each island must bond continuously to the cover around its opening. Otherwise water could escape into the magnet cavity, even with a perfectly sealed outside edge.

title: Bond the divider as well
speech: The divider is bonded too, so water must travel around the channel rather than take a shortcut. These gold areas are proposed joint regions, not existing braze features. The O ring grooves need to be removed or redesigned into suitable bonding lands, with the joining shop specifying the clearance and filler.

title: Close, fixture, and braze
bullets: Cover meets all eight seal regions and divider
Joining happens before magnets are installed
speech: The cover closes against the prepared lands. The parts are fixtured and brazed before any magnets or plastic components are installed. Filler bonds the mating surfaces into a continuous metal seal. The gold overlay shows the buried interface; it does not represent a thick gasket.

title: The joint becomes the seal
bullets: Magnet passages stay dry and accessible
Pressure and leak tests verify the result
speech: The finished body and cover become one permanent coolant enclosure. The magnet passages remain dry and accessible from the rear, and target changes do not open the water circuit. Pressure and leak testing must verify the joints. This animation explains the proposal; it does not change or qualify the existing CAD.
